text:
jordan: quick note from today's benchmark sweep: onboarding fenris-int4 vs fenris-fp16. streaming funcall conformance differs on structured output compliance. int4 has slightly higher malformed-array errors (~0.9% -> fp16 0.1%) when we enable both batching and streaming.

lee_r: suspect KV-cache merge boundary plus quantized tokeniser. any failing sample?

jordan: yep. here's one:
```
partial stream: '{"action":"search","args":[{"q":"pizza"},'
next chunk: ' {"q":"sushi"}]}'
```
The boundary split leaves an extra comma at end of first chunk leading to double commas after naive concatenation. parser errors.

oli: might be safer to join chunks and run a tolerant NDJSON-aware parser that tolerates a trailing comma when reconstructing arrays. but careful: trailing commas are not valid JSON and could mask a real malformed generator.

jordan: plan: implement tolerant rejoin with strict validation fallback. algorithm: 1) concat nearby chunks up to 60ms, 2) attempt strict parse, 3) if fails, try small tolerant repairs: remove trailing commas before closing brackets, remove leading control chars, then reparse. emit metric parse.repair_attempts and parse.repair_success.

lee_r: add audit log of repaired payloads to s3 for later analysis. also ensure we limit repair attempts per request to avoid expensive CPU cycles.

jordan: will add repairs cap=2 and max_repair_bytes=4096. test harness: 
```bash
python tests/repair_harness.py --model fenris-int4 --seed 7 --requests 20000
```
This shows repairable errors reduce schema.fail_rate from 0.9% to 0.15% in preliminary runs.

patch-bot: branch created: fenris/stream-repair (build queued).

oli: good. also run evaluation of downstream tool execution divergence: replay 10k repaired streams both repaired and unrepaired to ensure no semantic difference.

jordan: will do. aim for dogfood next week.
